output.myth: The cod of the deep shelf was old when Hesk first wound her string. Each ring on its scale is a year it swam through: a hard winter, a bad catch, a child born on the rock. When Aun cut the string and the sky went loose, the cod did not notice. It only went on, slow and grey. Orrun the Deep-Whale is older still, but he does not count, so the cod is the one the elders trust. They go down with a line and a knife and read the rings by lamplight, and the number is different every year, which the elders say is the cod's joke. The bright star at its eye marks the last year anyone managed to read. The rest of its rings are up in Vel, lit one at a time. Hesk says nobody will reach the end of the count, and that this is how she knows the cod is still swimming.
output.verse:
Count the rings slowly,
the old cod turns through cold deep,
each ring a year lived.
